# dznrm2

> Computes the Euclidean norm of a complex double-precision floating-point vector.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dznrm2 from '@rreusser/blahpack/blas/dznrm2';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dznrm2( N, x, strideX ) → number
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of indexed elements |
| `x` | `Complex128Array` | Input array |
| ↳ `strideX` | `integer` | Stride length (in complex elements) |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: number of elements in input vector(s)
- `x`: complex vector with N elements

</details>

**Returns** `number`: Euclidean norm

**Throws**

- `RangeError` first argument must be a nonnegative integer

### Strided (strided) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dznrm2.strided( N, x, strideX, offsetX ) → number
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of indexed elements |
| `x` | `Complex128Array` | Input array |
| ↳ `strideX` | `integer` | Stride length (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetX` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index (in complex elements) |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: number of elements in input vector(s)
- `x`: complex vector with N elements

</details>

**Returns** `number`: Euclidean norm

**Throws**

- `RangeError` first argument must be a nonnegative integer

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `dznrm2()` corresponds to the reference BLAS routine [`DZNRM2`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/BLAS/SRC/dznrm2.f90).

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import dznrm2 from '@rreusser/blahpack/blas/dznrm2';

// Euclidean norm of a complex vector:
const x = new Complex128Array( [ 3.0, 4.0, -6.0, 8.0, 0.0, 0.0 ] );

// Using the standard interface:
let out = dznrm2( 3, x, 1 );
console.log( out ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
// => ~11.180

// Using the strided interface (last two elements only):
out = dznrm2.strided( 2, x, 1, 1 );
console.log( out ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
// => 10.0
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference BLAS 3.12.0 source of `DZNRM2`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DZNRM2 returns the euclidean norm of a vector via the function name, so that

$$
\mathrm{DZNRM2} := \sqrt{ x^H \, x }
$$

### Further Details

Anderson E. (2017) Algorithm 978: Safe Scaling in the Level 1 BLAS ACM Trans Math Softw 44:1--28 https://doi.org/10.1145/3061665

Blue, James L. (1978) A Portable Fortran Program to Find the Euclidean Norm of a Vector ACM Trans Math Softw 4:15--23 https://doi.org/10.1145/355769.355771

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
